stimulus.title: Attendance at a street festival
stimulus.html:
A town counts the people who attend its street festival each day. The table gives the attendance AA, in hundreds of people, on selected days dd of the festival, where d=1d = 1 is the first day. The attendance is modeled by the quadratic function A(d)=ad2+bd+cA(d) = ad^2 + bd + c, whose graph passes through the three data points.
Attendance A, in hundreds of people, on day d of the festival
dd (day)147
AA (hundreds of people)4.29.68.4

parts.label: A(i)
parts.prompt: Use the given data to write three equations that can be used to find the values of the constants aa, bb and cc in the expression for A(d)A(d).

rubric.point: Three correct equations, one for each data point, with the input squared in the <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> term
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a + b + c = 4.2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>16</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16a + 4b + c = 9.6</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>49</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">49a + 7b + c = 8.4</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(1)^2 + b(1) + c = 4.2</annotation></semantics></math> and so on

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a + b + c = 4.2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>16</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16a + 4b + c = 9.6</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>49</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">49a + 7b + c = 8.4</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: Find the values of aa, bb and cc as decimal approximations.

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.366667</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = -0.366667...</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3.633333</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = 3.633333...</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.933333</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = 0.933333...</annotation></semantics></math>, each correct to three decimal places (rounded or truncated); all three needed
accept: values truncated to three decimal places
values from a calculator system solver or quadratic regression on the three points

parts.sample: Solving the system with a calculator: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.366667</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = -0.366667</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3.633333</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = 3.633333</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.933333</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = 0.933333</annotation></semantics></math>. These values are stored in the calculator and used in every later part.

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: Find the average rate of change of AA over the interval 1≤d≤71 \le d \le 7. Express your answer using correct units.

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7</annotation></semantics></math> hundred people per day, with the difference quotient shown and units
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{A(7) - A(1)}{7 - 1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>8.4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4.2</mn></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{8.4 - 4.2}{6}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0.7</annotation></semantics></math> hundreds of people per day

parts.sample: The average rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 7]</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{A(7) - A(1)}{7 - 1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>8.4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4.2</mn></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{8.4 - 4.2}{6}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0.7</annotation></semantics></math> hundred people per day.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: The average rate of change from part B(i) is the slope of a secant line. Use this secant line to estimate the attendance on day d=5d = 5. Show the work that leads to your answer.

rubric.point: An estimate of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7</annotation></semantics></math> hundred people from a point on the secant line through <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 4.2)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8.4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(7, 8.4)</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>0.7</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(1) + 0.7(5 - 1)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>4.2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 4.2 + 2.8</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 7</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7</annotation></semantics></math> hundred, or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>700</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">700</annotation></semantics></math> people, with the secant-line work

parts.sample: The secant line through <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 4.2)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8.4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(7, 8.4)</annotation></semantics></math> has slope <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7</annotation></semantics></math>, so it is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4.2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0.7</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 4.2 + 0.7(d - 1)</annotation></semantics></math>. At <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d = 5</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4.2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0.7</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.2 + 0.7(4) = 7</annotation></semantics></math>. The estimate is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7</annotation></semantics></math> hundred people.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: The town wants to use AA to plan for later days. Determine the largest day dd for which the model gives a reasonable attendance, and explain, using the model, why the model should not be used for days after that.

rubric.point: The bound <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>10.160</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d \approx 10.160</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(d) = 0</annotation></semantics></math> (found with a calculator, from the stored model)
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10.160</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d = 10.160</annotation></semantics></math> or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>10.1596</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10.1596</annotation></semantics></math> truncated or rounded to three places

"the model is reasonable for <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>10.160</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 \le d \le 10.160</annotation></semantics></math>"

rubric.point: A reason in context tied to the model: after that day the model gives negative attendance, which is impossible
accept: "<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(d) < 0</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>></mo><mn>10.160</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d > 10.160</annotation></semantics></math>, but attendance cannot be negative"
the model is decreasing after its maximum and reaches 0, so it cannot describe a crowd after that day

parts.sample: Graphing the stored model and finding its zero gives <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(d) = 0</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>10.160</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d \approx 10.160</annotation></semantics></math>. The model is concave down: after its maximum near <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4.955</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d = 4.955</annotation></semantics></math> it decreases, and for <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>></mo><mn>10.160</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d > 10.160</annotation></semantics></math> it gives <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(d) < 0</annotation></semantics></math>, a negative number of people, which cannot happen. So the model gives reasonable attendance only up to about day <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>10.160</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10.160</annotation></semantics></math>, and it should not be used after that.
